description: ANDES is an open-source Python package for power system modelling and simulation, and the dynamic simulation engine of the CURENT Large-scale Testbed. It offers five analysis routines, Newton-Raphson power flow, time-domain transient stability simulation with an implicit trapezoidal method, eigenvalue analysis, continuation power flow for voltage stability limits and state estimation, and a library of more than one hundred dynamic models including synchronous generators, governors, exciters, stabilisers, second-generation renewable models and distributed energy resources, defined symbolically. The package is written and maintained by Hantao Cui with contributors. It is location independent: cases are loaded from PSS/E RAW and DYR files or its own formats for any system. It is distributed on PyPI and conda-forge (version 2.0.0, March 2026, Python 3.11 or newer) with source on GitHub and documentation at docs.andes.app, under the GNU GPL version 3 or later at no cost. Caveats: electromagnetic transient simulation is not among its listed routines, so such studies need tools such as model-dpsim, and model fidelity depends on the dynamic data supplied. Simulation uses are network flow, transient stability and cascading failure analysis for resilience studies. Related records: it complements model-pandapower for steady state and model-dpsim for electromagnetic transients.
